rules.localIntel: Hand-curated from primary sources: each item was read at its own source on the date shown, states only what that source says, and quotes it where a quote is given. Where a source does not settle something (a winner, an end date) the item says not verified. Every link is re-checked on each daily build; an item whose source has gone is withdrawn until it is re-sourced. This is not a census: it lists the contracts, formularies and papers found and read, not every one that exists.
rules.frameworks: NHS Supply Chain framework names matching /(digital diagnostic solutions|radiotherapy it solutions)/i. NHSSC names a framework after its clinical category, so the name is the key; the CBU category field is far too broad to filter on. This is the one speciality in the Hub with no single buying route, and this panel shows the two NHS Supply Chain frameworks that do reach it — Digital Diagnostic Solutions and Radiotherapy IT Solutions. It cannot show the rest, because the rest are not NHS Supply Chain agreements: all four pages of the contract launch brief index were listed on 11/09/2026, 140 briefs, and no brief covers an electronic patient record, a GP clinical system, cyber security, networking or enterprise software. Those move through NHS Shared Business Services SBS10515 Tech Devices – Link 4, the NHS England Buying Catalogue, and Government Commercial Agency agreements including G-Cloud 15 (RM1557.15, live since 6 August 2026), none of which this feed covers. The award rows are correspondingly small: across the whole digital patch in the month to 10 September 2026 the median published award value was £21,911, and one £100m teleradiology framework modification was 98.4% of the total. The big money on this patch does not appear as a contract notice at all — it moves as capital business cases inside NHS England's Frontline Digitisation programme, as framework call-offs under a Unique Reference Number, and as G-Cloud awards without competition. An empty or short panel here is the honest answer, not a gap.
rules.suppliers: Every supplier NHS Supply Chain names on the frameworks above, resolved to one name per company through the Hub's alias registry, and ordered by how many of this speciality's frameworks they appear on. That count is the only claim made. It is not a ranking of size or share. Where NHS Supply Chain spelled a company two ways across its own pages, both spellings are shown against the one entry. This is the one speciality in the Hub with no single buying route, and this panel shows the two NHS Supply Chain frameworks that do reach it — Digital Diagnostic Solutions and Radiotherapy IT Solutions. rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(electronic patient record|EPR|electronic health record|patient administration system|clinical systems?|electronic prescrib\w*|ePMA|electronic document management|EDMS|EDRM|e-?observations?|cyber ?security|cyber essentials|interoperab\w*|clinical decision support|digital dictation|speech recognition|health information exchange|electronic staff record|digital diagnostic solutions)\b/i. NO EXCLUSION LIST IS APPLIED, because every notice this pattern matched was read one by one and all of them are this speciality. The loose terms that would have needed excluding were refused from the pattern above instead of admitted and then argued with. No CPV family corroborates this speciality: not one matching notice in this data carries a CPV code specific to it, so none is claimed. A CPV code could never admit a notice on its own in any case, because a notice carrying a basket of them is filed under all and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: No Drug Tariff part applies to this speciality. Part IX reimburses dressings and elastic hosiery (IXA), incontinence appliances (IXB), stoma appliances (IXC) and elastic hosiery (IXR); nothing on this patch is listed there, so the panel carries no tariff rather than reaching for the nearest part.
rules.directorySuppliers: Companies the Hub's own supplier directory files under this speciality, from the speciality labels on each company's directory record, resolved through speciality-label-map.json and speciality-map.json (Compare ids: digital, it). They are labelled DIRECTORY-TAGGED because the tag is the Hub's filing of a company's range, not a procurement record: being listed here is not evidence of a contract or of volume, and the list is not a census of the market. A company that is also on this speciality's own frameworks is listed once, with the framework-named suppliers, and marked as also directory-tagged. WHERE A COMPANY IS ON ANOTHER FRAMEWORK: where a directory-tagged company is named on an NHS Supply Chain framework that is not counted as this speciality's, it is still listed, with that framework named against it and linked, so it is not lost from the page. 43 of the 61 listed here carry such a note. Framework names and links come from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs as held in frameworks.json; an agreement the directory records from another buying organisation, such as an NHS Shared Business Services framework, is shown as the directory states it.
rules.gpPrescribing: No BNF section is mapped to this speciality, so no GP prescribing market is sized here rather than borrowing a neighbouring page's.
rules.mhraDsu: MHRA does not tag Drug Safety Updates to this area: no GOV.UK therapeutic-area facet maps to this speciality. That is a fact about how GOV.UK files them, not a finding that there are no safety updates relevant to it.
rules.digitalLane: A Find a Tender or Contracts Finder notice is in this lane when the buyer name is an NHS body (contains "NHS", "Integrated Care Board" or "Health Board"; bare "Trust" is not a match) AND a Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) code on the notice begins 48 (software package and information systems) or 72 (IT services). An Atamis opportunity carries no CPV code, so its own Category text stands in: a software, information systems or IT services category, or a title naming a clinical digital system. Every Atamis authority is an NHS body by construction. CPV 48 and 72 are bought for payroll, finance, human resources and office systems as much as for clinical ones, so a lane row is not a claim of health technology. A row is flagged clinical only when its TITLE names a clinical system or a regulated digital product (electronic patient record, electronic prescribing, picture archiving and communication system (PACS), laboratory information management system (LIMS), artificial intelligence (AI), ambient voice, virtual ward, remote monitoring and the other terms in scripts/digital_lane_rules.py). Bare 'software', 'digital', 'IT' and 'licence' never flag a row. The speciality page shows clinical rows only. A call-off under a framework is not a notice, and most digital money in the NHS moves as framework call-offs, capital business cases and G-Cloud awards without competition. This lane is therefore a floor, not a census: an absence here says nothing about the buyer or the market. Contract values, where shown, are the notice's own and are not summed across rows. Shown here: the clinical rows only, up to 15 awards and every open notice and market engagement row. The full lane, with the rows left out, is data/digital-lane.json.

localIntel.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
localIntel.title: AI Airlock Phase 3: call for applications open
localIntel.fact: The MHRA's regulatory sandbox for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled medical devices opened its third phase on 6 October 2026, with applications made through the Phase 3 application form on the page. No closing date is given on the page. Phase 2 completed in May 2026 with 7 innovators across 3 regulatory challenges. The government response of the same day gives an applicant webinar on 22 October.
localIntel.quote: The MHRA announced on 6th October 2026 the launch of the third phase of the AI Airlock.
localIntel.use: The named route for an AI-enabled device maker to test a regulatory question with the regulator before market. Cohort members named on the MHRA's cohort pages are companies with an active regulatory conversation.

localIntel.title: Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC): refreshed form; previous form retired from 6 April 2026
localIntel.fact: NHS England's refreshed DTAC form has a 25% reduction in questions and is de-duplicated with the Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT) and the pre-acquisition questionnaire. The page states the previous version of the form should not be used from 6 April 2026 onwards. DTAC covers clinical safety, data protection, technical security, interoperability, and usability and accessibility. Page last edited 21 September 2026.
localIntel.quote: The previous version of the DTAC form should not be used from 6 April 2026 onwards.
localIntel.use: The assurance form an NHS buyer in England asks a digital health supplier to complete. A supplier still sending the pre-April 2026 form is sending one the owner has retired.

localIntel.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) and ministers
localIntel.title: Government accepts all 44 recommendations of the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare
localIntel.fact: On 6 October 2026 the government confirmed it will accept all 44 recommendations of the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare (published 10 September). The MHRA is committed to issue draft guidance by December 2026 on a new approach to managing changes to artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled medical devices, and will begin next year by consulting on how to qualify and classify AI-enabled devices.
localIntel.quote: confirmed it will accept all 44 recommendations made by the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare
localIntel.use: The dated regulatory timetable for AI-enabled devices: draft change-management guidance by December 2026, then a qualification and classification consultation.
